 A dismal Manchester United performance ended in an emphatic defeat to Cesc Fàbregas’s completely dominant Como side 
  Updated  10m ago Simon Burnton Wed 21 Oct 2026 15.20 EDT First published on Wed 21 Oct 2026 11.15 EDT Share Key events 51m ago Final score: Como 4-1 Manchester United 
 54m ago GOAL! Como 4-1 Manchester United (Zirkzee, 90+1 mins) 
 1h ago GOAL! Como 4-0 Ohno (Ramon, 76 mins) 
 1h ago GOAL! Como 3-0 Manchester United (Paz, 57 mins) 
 2h ago GOAL! Como 2-0 Manchester United (Douvikas, 49 mins) 
 2h ago Half time: Como 1-0 Manchester United 
 3h ago GOAL! Como 1-0 Manchester United (Paz, 2 mins) 
 4h ago The teams! 
 4h ago Preamble 
 Bruno Fernandes reacts after Nico Paz scores Como’s third goal of the game. Photograph: Alessandro Garofalo/Reuters View image in fullscreen Bruno Fernandes reacts after Nico Paz scores Como’s third goal of the game. Photograph: Alessandro Garofalo/Reuters Simon Burnton Wed 21 Oct 2026 15.20 EDT First published on Wed 21 Oct 2026 11.15 EDT Share Key events 51m ago Final score: Como 4-1 Manchester United 
 54m ago GOAL! Como 4-1 Manchester United (Zirkzee, 90+1 mins) 
 1h ago GOAL! Como 4-0 Ohno (Ramon, 76 mins) 
 1h ago GOAL! Como 3-0 Manchester United (Paz, 57 mins) 
 2h ago GOAL! Como 2-0 Manchester United (Douvikas, 49 mins) 
 2h ago Half time: Como 1-0 Manchester United 
 3h ago GOAL! Como 1-0 Manchester United (Paz, 2 mins) 
 4h ago The teams! 
 4h ago Preamble 
 10m ago 15.20 EDT And with that, I’m off. Here’s Jamie Jackson’s match report again. Bye!
 Como destroy dismal Manchester United as humbling defeat piles pressure on Carrick Read more Share 16m ago 15.14 EDT Here are some snippets from Michael Carrick’s post-match interview: 
 double quotation mark It was more than disappointing. I think everybody’s got to take responsibility for that. I’ll take responsibility for the overall team and performance, it stops with me and I’m fine with that. But as a supporter of this football club, to see a performance like that is unacceptable, I have to say.
 I’ll look at what we’ve done. It’s the motivation and the purpose and the intensity of a game of football that you have to bring. We didn’t bring that today. You can’t choose when you want to perform or you don’t, when you give absolutely everything and when perhaps you don’t.
 I care an unbelievable amount about the supporters. They’re the heartbeat of this football club and always will be. I’ve got to apologise for the performance. Everything they’ve done to get here tonight, for them to watch that performance tonight, I feel for them.
 Tonight’s not about me. It’s about digesting the game, and how it went. That’s the most important thing right now.
 Share 19m ago 15.11 EDT I assume this is a wave of apology rather than farewell.
 View image in fullscreen Manchester United manager Michael Carrick apologises to the away fans at full time at Como. Photograph: Kieran McManus/Shutterstock Share 29m ago 15.00 EDT Thankfully we can rely on Jamie Jackson, who is lakeside for us tonight. And here is his match report!
 In sight of the Alps, a boat ride from George Clooney’s villa, Manchester United will hope, in what has been a terrible start to the season, that things do not get any worse.
 They can’t – for the team’s prospects, and Michael Carrick’s job security, because witnessed here by Lake Como was a humiliation of the three-times European champions by Cesc Fàbregas’s competition debutants, as United suffered their worst defeat in continental football since 1994.
 By 57 minutes this was over, as Como were 3-0 ahead, and Nico Paz had destroyed Carrick’s men with a scintillating display featuring two goals and the assist for Tasos Douvikas’s strike.
 Much more here:
 Carrick under more pressure as Manchester United humbled against Como Read more Share 34m ago 14.56 EDT It may take Manchester United fans some time to get over this performance/result, but TNT Sports have moved on pretty quickly. As I suppose they had to, given that loads more games start in five minutes, but doesn’t help me bring you the hottest reaction from a windswept, drenched Como.
 Share 37m ago 14.52 EDT The fun doesn’t end here! The 8pm games include Bayern Munich v Arsenal, which Scott Murray is monitoring here:
 Bayern Munich v Arsenal: Champions League – live Read more And also Aston Villa v Viking, Real Madrid v RB Leipzig and quite a lot more, which Sarah Rendell has to keep up with here:
 Aston Villa v Viking, Real Madrid v RB Leipzig and more: Champions League – live Read more Share 43m ago 14.46 EDT The good news for Michael Carrick is that Dimitar Berbatov, on TNT Sports, doesn’t say that United now have to beat Bournemouth on Sunday for him to stay in his job. The bad news for Carrick is that Berbatov’s reasoning is that Carrick might not still be in his job on Sunday. “I don’t think everyone was giving their best,” Berbatov says of this performance. “It didn’t look like that on the pitch. Como were having fun.”
 View image in fullscreen Manchester United's manager Michael Carrick leaves the pitch after his side’s heavy defeat to Como. Photograph: Antonio Calanni/AP View image in fullscreen Meanwhile his opposite number Cesc Fabregas is savouring a famous victory for Como. Photograph: Claudia Greco/Reuters Share Updated at  14.51 EDT 47m ago 14.43 EDT Manchester United’s next few games: 
 Sunday 25 October: Bournemouth (h)
 Saturday 31 October: Chelsea (a)
 Tuesday 3 November: Roma (h)
 Sunday 8 November: Aston Villa (h)
 Sunday 22 November: Liverpool (a)
 Share 49m ago 14.40 EDT United’s players wander over to apologise to whatever flimsy remnant of the travelling support isn’t already drowning their sorrows in a nearby hostelry.
 View image in fullscreen Manchester United's Mason Mount (second left), Noussair Mazraoui (left) and Diogo Dalot (second right) look dejected as they applaud their fans. Photograph: Alessandro Garofalo/Reuters Share Updated at  14.48 EDT 51m ago 14.39 EDT Final score: Como 4-1 Manchester United
 90+4 mins: Say what you like about this United performance, they completely dominated that period of stoppage time, and won it 1-0!
 Share Updated at  14.39 EDT 54m ago 14.36 EDT GOAL! Como 4-1 Manchester United (Zirkzee, 90+1 mins)
 United do have their consolation! Amad chips the pass into the box, Zirkzee escapes from his marker and brings it down beautifully, leaving himself with a pretty easy finish which he calmly completes.
 View image in fullscreen Joshua Zirkzee bags a consolation goal. Photograph: Antonio Calanni/AP Share Updated at  14.45 EDT 55m ago 14.34 EDT 90+1 mins: There’ll be three minutes of stoppage time, or thereabouts.
 Share 1h ago 14.33 EDT 89 mins: … Not like that they can’t. Lacey takes the corner, and three defenders line up at the near post to boot it clear, which one of them emphatically does.
 Share 1h ago 14.32 EDT 89 mins: Amad wins United a corner. Could they end the night with a consolation?
 Share 1h ago 14.31 EDT 87 mins: Lacey swiftly earns himself a booking. “The Guardian called for jeopardy in this competition. I think Man Utd have found it for you,” writes Ian Copestake. Their remaining Champions League fixtures: Roma (h), Sporting (a), Leipzig (h), Bayern Munich (h), Villarreal (a).
 Share 1h ago 14.29 EDT 86 mins: Another United substitution, Lacey replacing Mbeumo.
 Share 1h ago 14.28 EDT 84 mins: Kempf is booked, I think less for bringing down Amad than for being grumpy with the referee for giving the free-kick.
 Share 1h ago 14.27 EDT 82 mins: The last time Manchester United lost by four goals in Europe was more than 30 years ago, against a team that included Stoichkov, Romario and some chap called Guardiola.
 2 November 1994: Manchester United are thrashed in Barcelona Read more Share 1h ago 14.24 EDT 80 mins: Como bring on Smolcic, Ricci and Dossena, and take off Couto, Paz and Perrone.
 Share 1h ago 14.24 EDT 79 mins: Amass comes on for De Ligt, whose return from injury is the silver lining to tonight’s miserable, charcoal-grey cloud for United.
 Share 1h ago 14.22 EDT 78 mins: Como are hunting for a fifth, but Paz shoots too close to Lammens.
 Share 1h ago 14.22 EDT GOAL! Como 4-0 Ohno (Ramon, 76 mins)
 That is delicious. Ramon, the centre-back, spots Maguire creeping out of position and reckons he can get into that empty space before anyone notices. And turns out he was right. Kaiki Bruno sees him sprinting into an empty penalty area and sends in a perfect, precise cross, and Ramon hammers his header home from six yards!
 View image in fullscreen Jacobo Ramon heads home to give Como a fourth goal. Photograph: Mattia Ozbot/Uefa/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Ramon celebrates. Photograph: Claudia Greco/Reuters View image in fullscreen Noussair Mazraoui (left) and Amad Diallo (right) look dejected after the visitors go even further behind. Photograph: Piero Cruciatti/AFP/Getty Images Share Updated at  14.44 EDT 1h ago 14.18 EDT 73 mins: Zirkzee has brought a bit of extra pace and energy to the United team, if not any improvement in control. “Well, although it is quite funny (as a Liverpool fan) to watch a club swing from one manager to another chasing a dominance they once had (ahem), how much of the current malaise can be blamed on trying to keep up with the noisy neighbours across the city?” wonders Andy Flintoff (not that one). “Feeling that they have to do that has probably accelerated that swing and made the lurches more extreme.” I suppose it can’t have helped, though it seemed to have more of a positive effect on some other teams (if not their bank balances).
 Share 1h ago 14.14 EDT 69 mins: Kaiki Bruno and his exemplary caterpillar moustache comes on for Da Cunha.
 Share Updated at  14.14 EDT 1h ago 14.13 EDT 67 mins: Bruno Fernandes is taken off, which feels a bit like an admission of defeat. Zirkzee replaces him.
 Share 1h ago 14.10 EDT 66 mins: Amad shoots from 22 yards or so. The ball flies over Butez’s head and was probably also going over the bar but the keeper made sure.
 Share 1h ago 14.09 EDT 64 mins: Como bring Caqueret on for Baturina. United have been playing for the last five minutes or so with Mazraoui on the right and Dalot on the left.
 Share 1h ago 14.07 EDT 62 mins: Amad has been bright since he came on at half-time. He’s at the heart of a United attack but it ends with a blind cross, and a clearance. “Watching United at the moment, they look like a side completely in limbo, unable to move on,” writes Paul Flint. “The players surely know that Carrick is going sooner rather than later, and must be wondering about their futures. It doesn’t encourage in-game focus, however much they may be paid.”
 Share 1h ago 14.05 EDT 60 mins: Tielemans has a shot from the edge of the area, but it’s more of an apology than a challenge and Butez picks it up.
 Share 1h ago 14.03 EDT 59 mins: Paz tries another curler, this one from the edge of the D, but this one floats too close to Lammens.
 Share 1h ago 14.02 EDT GOAL! Como 3-0 Manchester United (Paz, 57 mins)
 Baleba hits a pass into Nico Paz’s shins just inside the United half and the ball runs beautifully into the Argentinian’s path, so he heads off, runs into the area, draws the keeper, and slides the ball across goal and in at the far post!
 View image in fullscreen Another smart finish from Nico Paz gives him his second goal of the night, and Como’s third. Photograph: Claudia Greco/Reuters View image in fullscreen Joy for Paz and the Como fans … Photograph: Alessandro Garofalo/Reuters View image in fullscreen Despair for Bruno Fernandes and his Manchester United teammates … Photograph: Alessandro Garofalo/Reuters View image in fullscreen And their manager Michael Carrick. Photograph: Kieran McManus/Shutterstock Share Updated at  14.15 EDT 1h ago 14.01 EDT 56 mins: An actually good United move ends with Mount flicking the ball towards Bruno Fernandes, but it’s intercepted.
 Share 2h ago 13.59 EDT 55 mins: Como should have had a third! Paz passes to Da Cunha, who shifts onto his left foot to open up a great shooting chance, 12 yards out, but then cuts across the ball rather than curling it with his instep, and it skews the wrong side of the post!
 Share 2h ago 13.58 EDT 54 mins: “I know watching United’s downfall has been fun for rival fans, I totally get that and don’t blame them for relishing it,” writes Lee Woolsey. “And I know this gets said a lot by fans about their team when they’re playing badly, but I’m sorry: this United team just look like they don’t care. They were a goal down after two minutes and the remaining 43 were an exercise in collective shoulder shrugging by a team of mercenaries assembled by a parasitic reign of witches. People DIED for this club. These players are a risible disgrace.” It’s very easy to blame the players, though. They aren’t well coached. They haven’t been well recruited. It’s the whole edifice.
 Share 2h ago 13.56 EDT 52 mins: “Not having a screen to watch this on, and just going on your mbm, I don’t think that Mount hasn’t been mentioned, is he doing as little as suggested?” wonders Martin Lancon. In brief, yes. United’s midfield hasn’t done very much. There were a couple of moments in the first half when Mount exchanged passes with Bruno Fernandes and the pair briefly looked pretty classy, but they haven’t achieved anything creatively. And as I type that Mount has a rubbish shot from 30 yards.
 Share 2h ago 13.55 EDT 50 mins: That’s just so easy. Paz carries the ball forwards, Douvikas runs into a massive space between De Ligt, who just didn’t see the run coming, and Maguire – the Dutchman stumbles at a crucial moment, but he was already out of the race – and finishes superbly!
 View image in fullscreen Tasos Douvikas (number 9) doubles Como’s lead with a smart finish. Photograph: Marco Luzzani/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Douvikas (third left) celebrates with his Como teammates. Photograph: Mattia Ozbot/Uefa/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Then heads back to his own half beside dejectected Manchester United players. Photograph: Marco Luzzani/Getty Images Share Updated at  14.06 EDT 2h ago 13.53 EDT GOAL! Como 2-0 Manchester United (Douvikas, 49 mins)
 A brighter restart for United, but in just over three minutes they’re two down!
 Share 2h ago 13.50 EDT 46 mins: Peeeeep! The game has restarted, and United have made a double halftimely substitution, Matheus Cunha and Andrey Santos going off, Diallo and Baleba coming on.
 Share 2h ago 13.43 EDT Just one goal, and that from a wonderful shot from outside the area, does not really reflect what has not been a tightly-contested game. United had one good chance, after just a couple of minutes, and even that came after some terrible ball control from Diogo Dalot and a lucky bounce off Perrone, for whom Dalot’s inability to control a football had been not so much unpredictable as unimaginable. I’m not sure what Uefa classify as an “attack” but Como have had 16 of them, and United five.
 Share 2h ago 13.34 EDT Half time: Como 1-0 Manchester United
 45+2 mins: It never rains but it pours, etc.
 View image in fullscreen Manchester United manager Michael Carrick heads back to the dressing room to plug in his hairdryer. Photograph: Marco Luzzani/Getty Images Share Updated at  13.40 EDT 2h ago 13.33 EDT 45+1 mins: One minute of stoppage time stands between United and the hairdryer treatment (or whatever it is they get these days when they’ve been rubbish).
 Share 2h ago 13.32 EDT 45 mins: An actual shot for United! Matheus Cunha gets the ball on the left-hand corner of the area, back to goal, then spins and sends a curling effort onto the roof of the net.
 Share 2h ago 13.31 EDT 43 mins: More work for Lammens, this time to keep out Baturina’s 20-yarder. He can’t hold it, but Douvikas is offside again as he reaches the rebound. “It’s mindblowing,” writes Joshua Keeling, “that Diogo Dalot is a professional footballer.”
 Share 2h ago 13.29 EDT 41 mins: United are saved by the offside flag! Douvikas is played through again, Lammens comes out and the striker goes over his leg … but the flag is up!
 View image in fullscreen Como's Tasos Douvikas (left) hits the deck in the area but the offside flag comes to Manchester United’s rescue. Photograph: Piero Cruciatti/AFP/Getty Images Share Updated at  13.42 EDT 2h ago 13.26 EDT 39 mins: Real chance! Yan Couto, no pressure on him, plays a lovely pass over the United defence to Douvikas, who brings it under control before wildly mishitting his shot, which skews off his shin high and wide when really he should have scored.
